draft.title: The Bible
card: The Christian Bible is a collection of writings in two main parts. Christians call these parts the Old Testament and the New Testament.
the Hebrew scriptures, which Christians share in part with Judaism. They were written before the time of Jesus.
the writings of the early church. They include the four Gospels, which tell of the life, death and resurrection of Jesus, and letters written to early Christian communities.
The four Gospels are Matthew, Mark, Luke and John. The letters, such as those of Paul, give guidance on belief and daily life.
draft.remember: The Bible joins the Hebrew scriptures with the early church's Gospels and letters.

a.q: Which part of the Christian Bible is shared in part with Judaism?
opts: The Old Testament, the Hebrew scriptures
The New Testament, the four Gospels
The New Testament, the early church letters
The Gospel of John, written about Jesus
a.why: The Old Testament is the Hebrew scriptures, which Christians share in part with Judaism. The Gospels and letters belong to the New Testament, which comes from the early church.
a.clue: Think about which writings came before the time of Jesus.

b.q: Sam reads a text in the Bible that Paul wrote to an early Christian community, giving advice on how to live. What kind of writing is it?
opts: A letter in the New Testament
A Gospel in the New Testament
A book of the Hebrew scriptures
A Gospel in the Old Testament
b.why: Writings sent to early Christian communities are letters, and they are part of the New Testament. A Gospel is different: it tells of the life of Jesus, so it is the most tempting wrong option.
b.clue: Was it written to a community, or does it tell the story of Jesus?

a.best: The Old Testament, the Hebrew scriptures

b.best: A letter in the New Testament
